title: Normalized ordinary tensor and action-unitor comparison of principal Koszul towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Write $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A/t^{n+1})_W$ for the actual completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use its projection-induced structural map to define the ordinary pullback $G$ on modules and termwise on unbounded cochain complexes [def-a1-integral-completed-tower-pullback-universes]. Use the sheaf tensor and direct-sum total cochain tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^{n+1}}R_W]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with the adjacent transition $(t,1)$, and put $H_W(P)=(P\otimes Q_{W,n})_{n\in\mathbf N}$ [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers]. Use the actual cone basis vectors and adjunction-unit generators of [def-a1-pulled-koszul-tower-normalization].

There is a family of isomorphisms of strict towers of cochain complexes $\theta_P:G(H_Y(P))\xrightarrow{\sim}H_X(GP)$, for every unbounded $R_Y$-complex $P$. Each isomorphism satisfies the specified KoszulNormalization equation: on either basis vector $e_i$, $i=-1,0$, in each total summand it sends $b\cdot G(x\otimes e_i)$ to $(b\cdot Gx)\otimes e'_i$, at every base-changed site object and for every local scalar $b$. For every chain map $f:P\to P'$ the strict tower maps satisfy $G(H_Y(f))\,\theta_{P'}=\theta_P\,H_X(Gf)$, in diagrammatic composition order. No goodness, boundedness, flatness or invertibility assumption on the completed structural map is imposed. This is only the ordinary tensor/action-unitor comparison; it asserts neither preservation of good complexes nor any quasi-isomorphism of augmentations.

proof.text: Write $\widetilde t$ for the inverse-image section of the completed uniformizer on $Y$. For every $m$, the composite $g^{-1}R_T\xrightarrow{c_g}R_{X}\xrightarrow{\pi_{X,m}}S_{X,m}$ is the inverse image of $\pi_{Y,m}$ followed by the constant coefficient map. That constant map sends the residue of $t$ to the same residue of $t$. Thus $c_g(\widetilde t)$ and $t$ have the same projection at every $m$; uniqueness of a map to the inverse limit gives $c_g(\widetilde t)=t$, hence $c_g(\widetilde t^n)=t^n$. The action unitor $GR_T\cong R_{X}$ sends $a\otimes b$ to $c_g(a)b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Under it $G(t^n)$ sends $c_g(a)b$ to $c_g(\widetilde t^na)b=t^nc_g(a)b$. This proves the required scalar normalization. Here Q_{W,n} uses exponent n+1; preservation of all powers applies to this positive exponent as well.

proof.text: Present the specified pullback by algebraic inverse image followed by scalar extension along the completed structural map. The supplied adjunction and uniqueness of left adjoints identify this presentation with CompletedTowerIndependent.pull. Transport the normalized ordinary tensor comparison along that isomorphism; its adjunction-unit equation identifies insertion of 1 with the generator used in KoszulNormalization. Use the ordinary cochain tensor comparison for the given completed ringed morphism. It gives $G(P\otimes Q_{Y,n})\cong GP\otimes GQ_{Y,n}$, naturally in both complexes, with the signed direct-sum total differential. Define $\phi_n:GQ_{Y,n}\to Q_{X,n}$ on both terms by $(ae_i)\otimes b\mapsto c_g(a)b e_i\prime$, with inverse $be_i\prime\mapsto e_i\otimes b$. These are mutually inverse balanced module maps. Step 1 gives the chain equation $c_g(\widetilde t^{n+1}a)b=t^{n+1}c_g(a)b$, so $\phi_n$ is a chain isomorphism. Compose the cochain comparison with $1_{GP}\otimes\phi_n$ to define $\theta_{P,n}$. In the coefficient-last convention of the item its value is $((x\otimes e_i)\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes b)\otimes e_i\prime$: the cochain comparison inserts $1$ into the second factor and $\phi_n$ takes that basis to $e_i\prime$. The degree-zero coefficient $b$ passes no nonzero-degree factor. Explicitly, for $x\in P^p$ the two differential contributions on either path are $(d x\otimes b)\otimes e_i\prime$ and $(-1)^p(x\otimes b)\otimes d(e_i\prime)$. Thus there is no additional sign.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, proof: isomorphism of total complexes; Tag 03EL for its ordinary constituents. The two-term unitor and sign calculation are explicit.

proof.text: For the adjacent Koszul transition, $\phi_nG(t,1)$ and $(t,1)\phi_{n+1}$ agree in degree $-1$ by $c_g(\widetilde t a)b=t c_g(a)b$, and in degree zero both send $a\otimes b$ to $c_g(a)b$. Naturality of the cochain tensor comparison in its second argument therefore gives $\theta_{P,n}G(1_P\otimes(t,1))=(1_{GP}\otimes(t,1))\theta_{P,n+1}$. Every arrow of the inverse sequence indexed by n >= 0, with exponent n+1 is a composite of adjacent arrows, so these are isomorphisms of strict towers. For a chain map $f:P\to P\prime$, naturality in the first argument gives the other square; on a local generator both paths send $((x\otimes e_i)\otimes b)$ to $(g^{-1}f(x)\otimes b)\otimes e_i\prime$. Hence the strict tower isomorphisms are natural for all the stipulated chain maps. No goodness or invertibility assumption was used in steps 1--3; the resulting family is defined on every unbounded complex.

lean.statement:
theorem pulled_koszul_tower_normalized_iso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ θ : ∀ P : CochainComplex (CompletedTowerIndependent.Modules l E Y) ℤ,
        (diagramPull l E g).obj (H l E Y P) ≅ H l E X ((G l E g).obj P),
      (∀ P, KoszulNormalization l E g P (θ P)) ∧
      (∀ {P P' : CochainComplex (CompletedTowerIndependent.Modules l E Y) ℤ}
        (f : P ⟶ P'),
        Functor.whiskerRight (sourceTowerMap l E Y f) (G l E g) ≫ (θ P').hom =
          (θ P).hom ≫ sourceTowerMap l E X ((G l E g).map f))
